items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: I came in Cab Calloway’s band with all these giants, Ben Webster, and Cab, and Doc Cheatham

ctx.x: I got on this Pullman, and there was all these great musicians on there, Doc Cheatham, Keg Johnson, Foots Thomas and all these guys. And I said Keg Johnson got me the gig, he recommended me, and I said to Keg, I say, “Keg, I didn’t ask Cab about no money or nothing,” I say, “He just told me to be here at nine o’clock.” He say, “Everybody in this band makes $100 a week.” I almost fainted. I almost fainted. I said I’ll be a millionaire in two months.
Well, and sure enough you are.

items.title: Doc Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 28, 1995
items.q: subject of a recent Nightline interview with fellow jazz veterans Milt Hinton and Lionel Hampton

ctx.x: Doc Cheatham’s remarkable career in jazz reads like a fairy tale. Born Aldolphus Cheatham in 1905, he grew up in Nashville and took up the sax and trumpet at an early age. His first playing experience was at the Bijou Theater where he played behind Bessie Smith, later recording on the soprano sax with another blues great, Ma Rainey.
